I would also ask Mr. Mango to explain the discrepancy between his copy of the tax return and the one filed with the IRS, and to provide any additional information that may be relevant to the situation.

You should also review the tax return for any potential errors or omissions, such as incorrect income or expenses, and verify that all credits and deductions are properly claimed. I would also ask Mr. Mango to provide documentation for any credits or deductions that he is claiming, such as receipts for charitable donations or medical expenses.

If the discrepancy is due to an error on the part of the accountant, I would advise Mr. Mango to contact the accountant and request that they correct the error and resubmit the tax return. If the discrepancy is due to intentional misrepresentation, I would advise Mr. Mango to report the incident to the IRS and seek their assistance in resolving the issue.

It's also worth noting that Mr. Mango should be aware of the potential consequences of filing a false tax return, including penalties and fines. I would advise him to be cautious and to seek professional advice before taking any action.
